description.narrative: The War Childhood Museum was founded in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 2015 as a new approach to reconciliation through research, exhibition and education. The Swedish support was aimed to support the implementation of following activities: - An exhibition and online campaign on 25th anniversary of Srebrenica Genocide focusing on experiences of Children. This will be shown in Sarajevo and other cities. - Online and on-site educational workshops for Children from all over BiH to make them aware of the past history and how to build a better future for everyone. Aim: to reach and work with 1700 students, ages 9-19, coming from different parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina. - An online platform for education on human rights, democracy and peace building –lessons from Bosnia and Herzegovina. Target group: students from abroad, ages 17-25. Aim: The workshop is designed to explore new and participatory forms of remembrance through the work with a single group of students (max 15 participants) over the course of eight weeks. (This activity was never implemented due to lack of co-funding. All Swedish funds (500 000 SEK) were allocated to the first two activities.)

The War Childhood Museum was founded in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 2015 as a new approach to reconciliation. It soon became an institution with a wide range of activities and a permanent museum in Sarajevo. Three main pillars of the WCM's activities are research, exhibition and education. There are many specific projects and initiatives within these three main groups which include: research activities (collecting and documenting the experience of people whose childhoods have been affected by war), production activities (production and editing of collected materials), exhibition activities (permanent, travelling and pop-up exhibitions, online campaigns, social media and media, etc), educational activities (group visits to permanent exhibition, workshops with school children and teachers).
War Childhood Museum is a new partner of the Embassy of Sweden in Sarajevo but the musuem and exhibition is well know and very well thought of. The Swedish support aims to support the implementation of following activities:
- Online and on-site educational workshops for Children from all over BiH to make them aware of the past history and how to build a better future for everyone. Aim is to reach around 1100 Children through this activity. - An exhibition and online campaign on 25th anniversary of Srebrenica Genocide focusing on experiences of Children. - An online platform for education on human rights, democracy and peace building – lessons from Bosnia and Herzegovina.

War Childhood Museum grundades i Bosnien och Hercegovina år 2015 som en metod för bearbetning och försoning. Det blev snart en institution med ett brett utbud av aktiviteter och ett permanent museum i Sarajevo. Tre huvudpelare i museets verksamhet är forskning, utställning och utbildning. Det finns många specifika projekt och initiativ inom dessa tre huvudgrupper vilket inkluderar: forskningsaktiviteter (insamling och dokumentation av erfarenheter från människor vars barndom har påverkats av krig), produktionsaktiviteter (produktion och redigering av insamlat material), utställningsaktiviteter (permanenta, resande och pop-up-utställningar, onlinekampanjer, sociala medier och media, etc.), utbildningsaktiviteter (gruppbesök på permanent utställning, workshops med skolbarn och lärare).
War Childhood Museum är en ny partner för Sveriges ambassad i Sarajevo men museet och dess utställning är välkänt och välrenommerat. Sveriges stöd syftar till att stödja genomförandet av följande aktiviteter:
- Utbildningsworkshops, både online och på plats, för barn från hela Bosnien och Hercegovina för att göra dem medvetna om landets nutidshistoria och hur en bättre framtid för alla kan byggas. Syftet är att nå cirka 1100 barn genom denna aktivitet. - En utställning och onlinekampanj i samband med 25-års minnesdagen av folkmordet i Srebrenica med fokus på barns upplevelser. - En online-plattform för utbildning om mänskliga rättigheter, demokrati och fredsbyggande - utifrån erfarenheter från Bosnien och Hercegovina.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative: 66 workshops were carried out with 884 children participating. The workshops promoted responsible peace activism and understanding of it and brought new generations new visions of peace/reconciliation. Although the number of children participating was a bit under anticipated (due to the pandemic), WCM still consider it a success that they managed to attract 30 schools and almost 900 children during the Activity Period amid unusual circumstances. The feedback the WCM received from parents, teachers and children who participated in our workshops during this period remained consistently positive. An exhibition and online campaign #ChildrenAndGenocide was realized during the July and August 2020. This contributed to making all survivors feel they are part of a greater community, their stories important memories of the past. The Campaign and Exhibition reminded about the complexities of genocides and aimed to prevent future genocides. Feedback received from both survivors who participated and those who identified themselves with the stories shared through this campaign and exhibition confirmed that this campaign and exhibition made them feel as a part of a greater community whose experience is important. During the campaign 180 posts were published on Twitter, Facebook and Instagram channels of War Childhood Museum and Humans of Amsterdam. They reached 11 million people and received over 300,000 reactions. Although most of the reactions were just signs of grief or support, hundreds people wrote meaningful comments and sent us messages about learning and raised awareness about the consequences of genocide on children.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
